evals.prompt: Generate the trtllm-serve config for openai/gpt-oss-120b on 8x H200 SXM: ISL 1024, OSL 1024, concurrency 64, TP 8, objective Max Throughput. A trimmed TensorRT-LLM checkout (configs and a few docs only) is at /workspace/input/trtllm-mini/. There is no GPU, network or TensorRT-LLM install in this sandbox; do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: Exact database match: two recipes exist for (gpt-oss-120b, H200_SXM, 8 GPUs, 1024/1024, conc 64); the profile: throughput one (1k1k_tp8_conc64_throughput.yaml) is chosen to preserve Max Throughput and emitted unchanged. Response is Config -> Source -> Launch command (trtllm-serve openai/gpt-oss-120b ... --config <yaml>), with trust_remote_code called out as a trust boundary and max_num_tokens 20000 confirmed to exceed ISL + template overhead.
assertions: Uses the exact database match for (gpt-oss-120b, H200_SXM, 8 GPUs, ISL 1024, OSL 1024, concurrency 64) and, of the two recipes for that key, picks the `profile: throughput` one (`examples/configs/database/openai/gpt-oss-120b/H200/1k1k_tp8_conc64_throughput.yaml`) to preserve the Max Throughput objective, not the latency-profile file.

Emits that config's fields unchanged (e.g. `enable_attention_dp: true` with its attention_dp_config, `moe_config.backend: TRITON`, tensor_parallel_size 8, moe_expert_parallel_size 8, max_num_tokens 20000, max_seq_len 2068, free_gpu_memory_fraction 0.8) without hand-tuned edits or added fields such as a speculative_config.
Structures the response as Config, then Source (the database file path), then Launch command, with a launch command of the form `trtllm-serve openai/gpt-oss-120b ... --config <that yaml>`.
Calls out `trust_remote_code: true` as a trust boundary.
Confirms that max_num_tokens (20000) covers ISL 1024 plus chat-template overhead.

evals.prompt: Generate a trtllm-serve config for deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 on 8x B200: ISL 1024, OSL 1024, concurrency 192, TP 8, objective Max Throughput. Use the trimmed TensorRT-LLM checkout at /workspace/input/trtllm-mini/. There is no GPU, network or TensorRT-LLM install in this sandbox; do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: No exact match for concurrency 192; starts from a neighboring checked-in B200 1k/1k database recipe (conc 128 or conc 256), chosen with the Max Throughput objective in mind. The MTP speculative_config is copied verbatim from that one source (max_draft_len 3 from conc 128 or 1 from conc 256, never an interpolated value), max_batch_size comes from the source rather than the concurrency, and the answer is Config -> Source used as starting point -> a single What to benchmark list, with trust_remote_code called out.
assertions: Finds no exact database match for concurrency 192 and uses a neighboring checked-in DeepSeek-R1-0528 B200 1k/1k database config (concurrency 128 or 256) as the starting point, naming its path.
Explicitly takes the Max Throughput objective into account when choosing between the neighboring recipes (e.g. why the attention-DP conc-256 recipe, or the conc-128 recipe, fits).

Copies the MTP `speculative_config` block verbatim from that single source file (`decoding_type: MTP` with that file's `max_draft_len` - 3 for conc 128, 1 for conc 256), never an interpolated value such as `max_draft_len: 2` or a value mixed in from the other file.
Keeps max_batch_size from the chosen source config instead of deriving it from the requested concurrency (does not set it to 192).
Uses the interpolated response format: Config, then Source used as starting point, then a single 'What to benchmark' list of knobs to sweep.
Calls out `trust_remote_code: true` as a trust boundary.

evals.prompt: Generate a trtllm-serve config for nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8 on 4x H100 SXM: ISL 2048, OSL 256, concurrency 4, TP 4, objective Min Latency. A trimmed TensorRT-LLM checkout is at /workspace/input/trtllm-mini/. There is no GPU, network or TensorRT-LLM install in this sandbox; do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: No database entry exists, so the curated llama-3.3-70b.yaml is the starting point, and the response calls out that it is labeled Max Throughput, conflicting with Min Latency. Interpolated fields: tensor_parallel_size 4, max_num_tokens raised above 2048 (ISL 2048 + template overhead), max_seq_len ~ISL+OSL+overhead (2304 < x <= ~2560); legacy TensorRT-engine numbers are ignored. Ends with one What to benchmark list and calls out trust_remote_code.
assertions: Finds no database entry for this model and uses the curated `examples/configs/curated/llama-3.3-70b.yaml` as the starting point, naming it as the source used as starting point.
Explicitly calls out that the only checked-in Llama-3.3-70B config is labeled Max Throughput, which conflicts with the requested Min Latency objective.
Sets max_num_tokens above 2048 so a 2048-token prompt plus chat-template overhead is not rejected (the curated value of 2048 is insufficient for ISL 2048).
Sets max_seq_len to ISL + OSL + a chat-template allowance: greater than 2304 and no more than about 2560.

Does not use the values from docs/source/legacy/ (max_batch_size 96, max_num_tokens 12288, free-memory fraction 0.95), treating TensorRT engine-build numbers as not transferable to PyTorch-backend serving.
Ends with a single 'What to benchmark' list of knobs to sweep rather than per-field unverified tags, and calls out `trust_remote_code: true` as a trust boundary.

evals.prompt: Generate a trtllm-serve config for Qwen/Qwen3-32B (dense, BF16) on 2x H100 SXM 80GB (nvidia-smi reports 81,559 MiB per GPU), TP 2, ISL 8192, OSL 1024, concurrency 64, objective Balanced. Will concurrency 64 fit in KV cache? The model's Hugging Face config is at /workspace/input/qwen3-32b-hf/config.json (BF16 weights are about 65.5 GB in total) and a trimmed TensorRT-LLM checkout is at /workspace/input/trtllm-mini/. No GPU, network or TensorRT-LLM install in this sandbox; do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: No checked-in config exists for Qwen3-32B, so the config is interpolated and marked unverified. GQA KV per token per GPU = 2 x 64 x (8/2) x 128 x 2 B = 131,072 B, ~1.125 GiB per 9,216-token request; with the 0.90 HBM factor and ~32.75 GB of weights per GPU, roughly 32-37 requests fit, so concurrency 64 does not fit with BF16 KV (options: FP8 KV, TP 4, lower concurrency). max_num_tokens > 8192, max_seq_len ~9,216 + template overhead (not 40,960), single What to benchmark list.
assertions: Finds no checked-in database or curated config for Qwen3-32B in the trimmed checkout and therefore treats the result as interpolated/unverified (the Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE recipes are a different model).

Computes the per-token KV size per GPU with the GQA formula: 2 x 64 layers x (8 KV heads / TP 2) x 128 head_dim x 2 bytes = 131,072 bytes (128 KiB), i.e. about 1.125 GiB per 9,216-token request per GPU.

Estimates the maximum concurrent requests with the 0.90 HBM factor at roughly 32-37, concludes that concurrency 64 does not fit with BF16 KV at full ISL+OSL, names options to close the gap (e.g. FP8 KV cache, TP 4, or lower concurrency), and marks the formula-derived numbers as unverified.
Sets max_num_tokens above 8192 (ISL plus chat-template overhead) rather than the 8192 default.
Sets max_seq_len to ISL + OSL + a chat-template allowance (greater than 9216 and at most about 10,240), not the 40,960 max_position_embeddings.
Uses the interpolated response format with a single 'What to benchmark' list of knobs to sweep rather than per-field unverified tags.

Produces separate context-server and generation-server configurations (each with a KV-cache transfer / cache transceiver setting) plus a disaggregated orchestration/router config, rather than a single aggregated trtllm-serve config.
